Keyrook brand

One look for every Keyrook product — Keyrook Authenticator, the website, and the apps after it. Everything on this page is generated from packages/brand/src; the files it shows are in packages/brand/assets, and packages/brand/brand.css gives any page the same colours and movements.

The crow

A rook is two things: the chess piece the name suggests, and a bird of the crow family. Crows are known for picking things up and keeping them. Ours keeps a key. Its feathers are four crayons — the colours the product has always had — and its eye is the same yellow as the key.

Keyrook is drawn by hand: ink on paper, crayon colour, lines that wobble a little. It is plain and a bit rough on purpose. A security product that looks like a person made it is easier to trust than one that looks like a vault door.

Two drawings, by size

Below 32 px the compact crow is used: no feet, two broad feathers, a bigger key. At 16 px a foot is a fifth of a pixel and four feathers are one smudge. markFor(px) picks the right one.

Room and size

  • Clear space round the crow: at least the width of the key on every side.
  • Smallest: the crow at 16 px (compact), the lockup at 120 px wide. Below that, use the crow alone.
  • The wordmark is lettered, not typed. Never set "keyrook" in a font to stand in for it.

Don't

Recolour the crow
Stretch it
Use Google's colours
Busy ground, no sticker

The family

The crow is Keyrook's, and only Keyrook's. It appears where the brand itself speaks: the Keyrook account every product signs in to, the emails it sends, Keyrook's own site, and a small "by Keyrook" at the foot of a product's page. A product never wears it as its icon.

Each product has its own mark, drawn in the same hand with the same four crayons, so the family shows without one member borrowing another's face. Its name is Keyrook and what it does.

Keyrook — the brand
Keyrook Authenticator
The next product — its own mark

Keyrook Authenticator

The countdown asterisk the extension has always had — eight ticks round a centre, like the dial of the 30-second timer every code runs on, and like the asterisks that mask a password — redrawn by hand in Keyrook's crayons. They run blue, yellow, red, green clockwise from twelve — warm pair together, cool pair together: neither Google's order, in either direction, nor Google's colours, which is what keeps eight coloured ticks from reading as theirs. Below 32 px the compact drawing, straighter and thicker. authenticatorMarkFor(px) picks it.

Action is blue, danger red, warning yellow, success green — the same in the extension, the site and any app. Red, yellow and green at 500 are too light for text on paper; they colour marks and fills, and text uses the stop in the table, which holds 4.5:1.

Type

Keyrook has no handwriting font. The hand shows in what is drawn — the crow, the wordmark, lines and boxes. Words stay in the system's own faces, so all fifty languages look like one product, and none falls back to a stranger's font halfway through a sentence.

TextThe quick brown fox — Chữ tiếng Việt — 日本語 — العربية
Codes482 913

--kr-font-sans, --kr-font-mono. Codes, addresses and recovery keys are mono, straight and still: a person reads them and types them somewhere else.

Lines and boxes

Three pen weights for drawn things — --kr-line-hair 1.5px, --kr-line-pen 2px, --kr-line-marker 3px at a 24 px icon. A box is drawn by hand with .kr-sketch: four corners that are not quite the same.

A card drawn by hand.

Motion

Two movements belong to Keyrook, both from hand-drawn animation, and the plain ones under them.

Draw — a line drawn in by the pen, once
Boil — redrawn a hair out of place, a few times, then still
fast120msa press, a toggle
base200msa sheet opening, a toast
slow400msa screen arriving
draw700msa line drawn in
boil150ms × 3, 4 roundsa drawing settling in
easecubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1)
  • Drawings move; text a person must read never does. A code that wobbles is a code read wrong.
  • Movement is brief and on arrival. Nothing loops forever except where something is genuinely waiting.
  • Only transform and opacity: nothing that moves the layout round it.
  • prefers-reduced-motion stops all of it. brand.css already does.

Words

  • Keyrook is the brand, and names only what Keyrook products share: the account ("a Keyrook account"), the email sender.
  • Each product is Keyrook + what it does: Keyrook Authenticator. The name is never translated.
  • Plain and honest about limits. No "military-grade", no "unhackable".
  • Every word a person reads lives in a language file, the same keys in every language, so all languages say the same thing.

Using it

In a product in this repository:

import { markFor, markSvg, CRAYON } from '@keyrook/brand';
@import '…/packages/brand/brand.css';   /* --kr-* and .kr-boil, .kr-draw, .kr-sketch */

Anywhere else: the files in packages/brand/assets, and the values on this page.
